title: Abstract Reasoning Pro
shortDescription: Advanced non-verbal matrix reasoning beyond Spatial Intelligence — denser rule sets, higher ceiling.
longDescription: Abstract Reasoning Pro is built on the Raven's Progressive Matrices paradigm (Raven, 1936) — the archetypal non-verbal matrix-reasoning test, still one of the most widely used non-verbal intelligence measures today. Each item shows a 3x3 grid following a rule across shape, color, rotation, and/or count; you identify the rule and pick the option that completes the missing cell. This version runs denser than Spatial Intelligence's matrix section — most items combine two or three simultaneously-changing attributes rather than one.
sourceNote: Every grid and answer option is a real, programmatically generated and rendered SVG (embedded as data URIs in question.media and option.imageUrl — no external asset pipeline needed) — not a text description standing in for an image, which is what blocked this assessment in earlier batches. Each item's rule (which attribute varies by row/column/diagonal) is applied in code to derive the correct cell, and every item was verified programmatically (exactly one option matches the derived correct attributes) before being included; several were also spot-checked visually by rendering to PNG. Raven's Progressive Matrices itself is a copyrighted, commercially published instrument (its current edition), so these are original grids implementing the same paradigm and rule families (constant-in-a-row/column, pairwise progression, distribution-of-three), not reproductions of the actual published matrices.

sections.name: Matrix Reasoning
sections.description: 3x3 grids following a rule across shape, color, rotation, and count.
sections.instructions: Identify the rule governing the grid, then choose the option that correctly completes the missing cell.

scoringDimensions.label: Abstract Reasoning
scoringDimensions.description: Non-verbal pattern reasoning across simultaneously-varying attributes.

resultRanges.title: Developing
resultRanges.description: Spotting a single rule is manageable, but grids with two or three attributes changing at once are difficult to fully untangle right now.
recommendations: Work through one attribute at a time — check shape first, then color, then rotation, rather than all at once
Practice on Spatial Intelligence's single-attribute matrices before returning here
For each row and column, name out loud what stays the same and what changes

resultRanges.title: Average
resultRanges.description: Two-attribute grids are usually solvable, but three-attribute or distribution-of-three items are still error-prone.
recommendations: When a grid feels ambiguous, check whether the rule might be a row/column pattern rather than a simple repeat
Practice specifically on items where every row (or column) contains the same three values in different positions

resultRanges.title: Strong
resultRanges.description: Reliable across most rule types, including grids with two or three simultaneously-changing attributes.
recommendations: Push into distribution-of-three items specifically — they require checking rows AND columns, not just one
Time yourself to build speed once accuracy feels solid

resultRanges.title: Very Strong
resultRanges.description: Consistently identifies the governing rule quickly, even across dense, multi-attribute grids.
recommendations: This level of abstract pattern reasoning transfers directly to Fluid Intelligence Peak's even more novel rule types
Notice which specific rule family (row/column constant, progression, distribution) you solve fastest

resultRanges.title: Exceptional
resultRanges.description: Near-perfect performance across every rule type and density level tested.
recommendations: Try Fluid Intelligence Peak for even more novel, less familiar rule structures
This is a strong general-reasoning signal independent of specific knowledge or vocabulary
